title: Refine the back-in-stock alerts epic
context:
Refinement is on Thursday. The BU wants **back-in-stock alerts** on all brands: shoppers who land on an out-of-stock product can ask to be emailed when it's back. Today the backlog has one big item, **HB-115 "Back-in-stock alert sign-up on product page"**, with one line of description and no acceptance criteria.

Priya (tech lead): *"We can't estimate this as one thing. Can you bring it split into stories the team can actually finish in a sprint?"*

data.title: Facts you have
rows: 55% of product-page visitors are not logged in (guests)
Chemist & Co and Maison Parfum sell many products in several shades/sizes
Service emails go through the existing email platform; legal says an alert is a service email (no marketing consent needed)
Alerts expire after 90 days; no sign-up for discontinued products
A product-page sign-up mock-up is ready and linked in the epic

data.title: HB-115 as written today
rows: BU wants customers to sign up for an email when an out-of-stock product is back.

task: Split the epic into 4–8 vertical stories with a size estimate and at least one acceptance criterion each. Then assess HB-115 against the Definition of Ready.
constraints: Each story must deliver something a shopper can use or the business can measure
Do not split by technical layer (front end / back end)

parts.label: Your stories
parts.prompt: Write 4–8 stories. Estimate each (your best guess; the team will challenge it) and add at least one acceptance criterion.

parts.label: Definition of Ready check for HB-115
parts.prompt: Which Definition of Ready items does HB-115 fail today? Select all that apply.

options.label: Clear user story with a "so that"
options.feedback: It is a one-line BU wish with no user or benefit.

options.label: Estimated by the team
options.feedback: A BU guess is not a team estimate.

options.label: Dependencies known
options.feedback: Email platform, stock feed and legal input have not been checked.

options.label: Designs attached (UI change)
options.feedback: A mock-up is already linked in the epic, so this one passes.

options.label: Approved by the BU director
options.feedback: Not a Definition of Ready item: readiness is about clarity, not sign-off.

keypoints.label: Sending the alert when stock returns

rubric.full: Every story delivers usable value end to end
rubric.partial: Some stories are technical layers or tasks

rubric.full: Guest, variants, duplicates, discontinued, expiry all handled
Identified the 4 gaps and knew design passes
rubric.partial: Some gaps missed or wrong items picked

hints: Follow the shopper's journey: sign up → get the alert → manage it. Each step can be a story.
Look at the facts table: guests, shades, discontinued products and the 90-day expiry are each a slice or an acceptance criterion.

A good set: (1) logged-in sign-up, (2) guest sign-up with email, (3) send alert when back in stock, (4) per shade, (5) unsubscribe, (6) expiry after 90 days, (7) reporting. For the DoR: story, ACs, estimate and dependencies fail; design passes.
modelAnswer:
### Stories
| # | Story | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | As a logged-in shopper on an out-of-stock product, I want to ask to be notified, so that I don't have to keep checking | 3 |
| 2 | As a guest shopper, I want to leave my email for an alert, so that I can be notified without creating an account | 3 |
| 3 | As a shopper with an alert, I want an email when the product is back in stock, so that I can buy it before it sells out | 5 |
| 4 | As a shopper choosing a shade, I want the alert to be for that exact shade, so that I'm not told about a shade I don't want | 3 |
| 5 | As a shopper, I want to unsubscribe from an alert from the email, so that I stop receiving emails I no longer need | 2 |
| 6 | As the business, we want alerts to expire after 90 days, so that we don't email shoppers about products they've forgotten | 2 |
| 7 | As the BU eCommerce manager, I want to see sign-ups and orders from alerts, so that I can judge if the feature pays off | 2 |

**Example acceptance criteria (story 2)**
- Given the product is out of stock and I'm not logged in, when I submit a valid email, then I see a confirmation and the alert is stored.
- Given I already have an alert for this product, when I sign up again, then no duplicate is created and I see "You're already on the list".
- Given the product is discontinued, when I view it, then no sign-up is offered.

### Definition of Ready for HB-115
Fails: **user story**, **acceptance criteria**, **team estimate**, **dependencies** (email platform, stock feed, legal confirmation not checked).
Passes: **design** (mock-up linked). "BU director approval" is not a DoR item.
commonMistakes: Splitting into "API story" and "UI story", which deliver nothing on their own
Forgetting guests, even though they are 55% of visitors
Putting every rule into one giant story
Treating the BU guess of "8" as an estimate
